# A plain Go package kept by a dependency's own in-tree replace is
# copied into the export through that dependency's tree, so its
# same-named user calls need the full rewrite check: eject must refuse
# the call as ambiguous instead of letting the spelling rewrite steal it.

env GOPROXY=off
env GOTOOLCHAIN=local

cd deepmain
! logos eject -o out
stderr 'ambiguous EnableHTTP2ExtendedConnect'
! exists out
cd ..

-- deepmain/go.mod --
module example.com/h2kddeep

go 1.27

require (
	example.com/h2kddeepdep v0.0.0
	example.com/h2kdsub v0.0.0 // indirect
)

replace example.com/h2kddeepdep => ../deepdep

replace example.com/h2kdsub => ../deepdep/sub

-- deepmain/main.lgo --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"example.com/h2kddeepdep"
)

func main() {
	fmt.Println("deepmain ready:", deepdep.Serve())
}

-- deepdep/go.mod --
module example.com/h2kddeepdep

go 1.27

require example.com/h2kdsub v0.0.0

replace example.com/h2kdsub => ./sub

-- deepdep/dep.lgo --
package deepdep

import "example.com/h2kdsub"

func Serve() int {
	return sub.Run()
}

-- deepdep/sub/go.mod --
module example.com/h2kdsub

go 1.27

-- deepdep/sub/meter.go --
package sub

// Meter is a user type with the same opt-in name as the fork-only
// (*net/http.Server) method. The export copies this in-tree replacement
// through its parent dependency, so the rewrite would steal the call
// and the check must refuse it.
type Meter struct{ Hits int }

func (m *Meter) EnableHTTP2ExtendedConnect() { m.Hits++ }

-- deepdep/sub/sub.go --
package sub

import "net/http"

func Run() int {
	m := &Meter{}
	m.EnableHTTP2ExtendedConnect()
	return len(http.MethodGet) + m.Hits
}
